summary: An excerpt from a novel (labeled Book 3, part 8) in which Carly Grove, a single woman who could not conceive by in vitro, explains how she turned to adoption and then to an organization called Children of Light. During a filmed interview with the narrator, she describes failed adoption attempts, being referred to the group's clinic up the Hudson, and her dealings with its head, Dr. Alex Goddard. The narrator's probing questions suggest that something about the organization is unusual.
one_line: Carly Grove describes her failed adoption attempts and her dealings with the mysterious Children of Light organization and Dr. Alex Goddard.
key_facts: Carly Grove concluded that, after in vitro fertilization failed, if she wanted a baby she had to adopt.
Carly Grove got worked over by attorneys trying to adopt as a single mom before she heard about Children of Light.
Carly Grove described Children of Light as the place that can make it happen.
Carly Grove's main lawyer, Chuck, recommended she hock the family silver, take a Valium, and try Children of Light.
Carly Grove tried to adopt the baby of a woman in a Memphis jail, but that adoption fell through.
Children of Light first tried to get Carly Grove to check into its clinic up the Hudson to see if her 'condition' could be cured.
Dr. Alex Goddard is described by Carly Grove as a kinda spacey guy and the big-shot presiding guru at Children of Light's clinic.
Carly Grove said Goddard sort of mesmerizes you.
Carly Grove told Children of Light's staff she did not have the time for the clinic and that nothing could be done.
Goddard sent Carly Grove back to the staff after she said it was adoption or nothing, and she described this as 'Checkbook time.'
The interview is filmed with two 35-mm Panaflex cameras, a video camera and monitor, and a boom mike, with Tony and Sherry running the production.
The clap stick marked the start of the shoot as 'Scene one, take one, Carly Grove interview.'
The narrator asked Carly whether Children of Light seemed in any way unusual, and she shrugged off the question as though puzzled.
